key_insight: A hybrid front-surface nanocone plus absorber-embedded nanohole architecture boosts thin-film silicon solar-cell light trapping, reducing reflection and improving absorption across the spectrum.
engineering_relevance: This design offers a practical optical-geometry route to raise current generation and efficiency in thin-film Si cells while maintaining strong thermal robustness.
method: Optimize nanocone and nanohole geometry with FDTD optical simulations
Couple optical results to electrical device modeling under optimized doping
Evaluate coupled opto-electro-thermal behavior under non-isothermal conditions
evidence_signal: The optimized device reached 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, while retaining 95.21% efficiency up to 45°C.
watch_item: Fabrication complexity and alignment of nanoscale nanocones and embedded nanoholes may complicate scalable manufacturing and increase process variability.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
